errors.english: it means to be separated from the state of dependence
errors.why: མནོད་པ is the root text's word for harm (the commentary itself glosses it as གནོད་པ, the Sangha's penalties), not the state of dependence.

fix.find: it means to be separated from the state of dependence
fix.replace: it means [helping him] to be freed from the harm

errors.english: one must quickly be assisted and supported in separating from the injury and moving away from the punishment by the community of monks (Sangha)
errors.why: The pupil is the one who attends on and helps the preceptor or teacher, so that he is quickly freed from the penalty imposed by the Sangha; the pupil is not the one being helped.

fix.find: one must quickly be assisted and supported in separating from the injury and moving away from the punishment by the community of monks (Sangha)
fix.replace: the pupil should attend on him and help him to be quickly freed from the harm of penance and the like imposed by the community of monks (Sangha)

errors.english: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
errors.why: The root text says the teacher (གནས་) in turn does these things for the pupil, except asking permission.

fix.find: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
fix.replace: **He [the teacher] too does these things for him [the pupil], except asking permission.**

errors.english: while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher
errors.why: The commentary says the teacher (གནས་) also attends on and helps the pupil with bowl, robes and the rest; the only difference is that he does not ask the pupil's permission.

fix.find: while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher
fix.replace: the teacher too, except that he need not ask permission, must assist and support the pupil

errors.english: must not live without relying on a preceptor (Upādhyāya) or a resident teacher (Ācārya)
errors.why: This is a list of three things a monk of under ten years may not do: act as preceptor, act as a teacher who gives dependence, or live without dependence. The next sentence calls them 'these three'.

fix.find: must not live without relying on a preceptor (Upādhyāya) or a resident teacher (Ācārya)
fix.replace: must not act as a preceptor (Upādhyāya), act as a teacher of dependence (Ācārya), or live without dependence

note: The Vinaya passages are readable, but who does what between pupil and teacher is reversed twice, and the three prohibitions are mis-segmented.

errors.english: he should bless his mind with the thought
errors.why: In Vinaya, སེམས་ཀྱིས་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབ (adhiṣṭhāna) means to resolve or determine mentally, not to bless the mind.

note: A faithful rendering of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties.

errors.english: The arrogance generated by power is seen by those of equal or superior capability to be ineffective on the other side; it does not dwell in the hearts of the noble ones.
errors.why: The verse says that pride born of power does not stay in the hearts of the noble, because they look at others who are equal or superior in capability. The noble are the ones who look; 'ineffective on the other side' is not in the text.

fix.find: The arrogance generated by power is seen by those of equal or superior capability to be ineffective on the other side; it does not dwell in the hearts of the noble ones.
fix.replace: The arrogance generated by power does not dwell in the hearts of the noble ones, for they look upon others who are equal or superior in capability.

errors.english: by being skilled at distributing a considerable amount of meaningless things
errors.why: དོན་མ་ཡིན་པ here is anartha, harm: the unshared misdeeds bring no small harm. It does not mean distributing meaningless things.

note: The parables are rendered well, but the verse on pride born of power is misconstrued and the opening sentence is garbled.

errors.english: the final part enters into the third portion
errors.why: This is a grammatical point: in གང་རྣམས་ཀྱིས the ending applies to the third case (the instrumental). It does not refer to a 'third portion' of the ritual.

errors.english: "residing completely" refers to the holy life
errors.why: ཡོངས་སུ་གནས་པ is the Vinaya term parivāsa(-ika), a monk under probation (as the next side shows), not 'residing completely'.

note: The karman-completion argument and the boundary quotation are sound, but the grammatical and Vinaya technical terms are rendered literally and wrongly.

errors.why: In the patriarch list Upagupta's successor is Dhītika/Mecaka; Madhyāntika belongs to an earlier generation, so the note misleads.

note: A faithful rendering of the commentary on the authenticity of the Mahāyāna and its lineage of transmission.

errors.english: the knowledge of the third characteristic of a logical sign
errors.why: Continuing ཚུལ་ from the previous side, this is the sign possessing the three modes (trairūpya), not the third characteristic.

fix.find: the knowledge of the third characteristic of a logical sign
fix.replace: the knowledge of the sign possessing the three characteristics

note: The argument about niścita, anvaya and vyatireka is mostly well rendered; the opening term is misread.

errors.english: Harmonious factors are not those of a similar class
errors.why: The Tibetan glosses 'similar in property' AS 'those of similar kind'; the negation is added.

fix.find: Harmonious factors are not those of a similar class
fix.replace: Harmonious factors are those of a similar class

errors.english: means it does not abide in the cognition of the object of appraisal
errors.why: The gloss is positive: the lemma concerns what abides in the cognition of the object; the 'not' is added.

errors.english: it would be because the sequential itself appears as the (actual thing) the self-substance or reality of the object
errors.why: These are two separate lemma glosses ('if the other' = if the non-sequential appears; 'its own reality appears' = by the sequence itself appearing), merged here into one conditional claim.

note: A dense lemmatic commentary. The sequence/non-sequence glosses are mostly tracked, but one negation is added and some glosses are fused.

errors.why: The side ends with the first syllable of the next lemma (gtan tshigs); the words '2 lines' are an artifact, not in the Tibetan.
མི་བཤེས་པ here means strangers (not acquainted), as the gloss 'not seen before' shows, not 'unfriendly'.

note: A faithful rendering of the word-by-word compound analysis of the verses on skill in speech.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna) the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum transformed is the mantra's own (its series of successive moments), not a mental stream of consciousness.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on mantra efficacy is rendered soundly overall.

errors.english: the supreme essence of all things
errors.why: This qualifies the garland of commands (Skt. suvastu-vicitra-śobhā) as beautiful with excellent things; it does not mean 'the supreme essence of all things'.

note: The Tibetan verses are rendered faithfully. The interleaved Sanskrit is the original of the same verses and is rightly not translated twice.
